battle.name: 第三次英阿戰爭
battle.brief: 第三次英阿戰爭於1919年5月由英屬印度聯軍進入阿富汗而展開，戰線集中於阿富汗東境、喀布爾及通往首都的道路，最終迫使阿富汗接受停戰安排。德國陸軍於1870年列裝的婆塞德後膛砲，正式型號為Breech-loading cannon，是當時野戰炮兵體系中的火炮裝備。

kit.name: 婆塞德後膛砲
kit.history: 婆塞德後膛砲在德國陸軍中屬於野戰炮兵，用來執行火力壓制與正面支援，並與步兵及後勤單位共同構成師級地面作戰體系。

countries: 參戰國與戰區：1919年5月6日至8月8日，英國以英屬印度政府的名義，由英國皇家陸軍、印度軍及受英方指揮的印度土邦部隊，對抗由埃米爾哈比布拉汗統治的阿富汗埃米爾國。英軍在英屬印度西北邊疆省、俾路支、奎達與阿富汗東部作戰，先後涉及巴米揚、庫拉姆、霍斯特、哈里河、努魯茲等地；克什米爾方向並非主戰場。駐尼泊爾招募的廓爾喀營屬英屬印度軍建制，尼泊爾本身不是交戰國。英軍雖以飛機偵察並轟炸阿富汗軍事目標，地面部隊始終沒有進入喀布爾，因此這是一場以東阿富汗邊境據點、外圍山區與外交談判為主的有限戰爭。
countriesEn: Belligerents and theater: From 6 May to 8 August 1919, Britain fought through the Government of India, using British Army troops, the Indian Army, and forces from Indian princely states under British command, against the Emirate of Afghanistan under Emir Habibullah Khan. Operations took place across the North-West Frontier Province, Baluchistan, Quetta, and eastern Afghanistan, with fighting at Bamiyan, Kurram, Khost, the Hari River, and Nowruz; Kashmir was not the main theater. Gurkha battalions recruited in Nepal formed part of the Indian Army, but Nepal itself was not a belligerent. British aircraft reconnoitred and bombed Afghan military targets, but the ground force never entered Kabul, making this a limited war fought around frontier positions, mountain country, and diplomatic negotiations rather than a campaign for the Afghan capital.
people: 阿軍最高統帥是埃米爾哈比布拉汗。他自1901年起執掌阿富汗，既想維持國家軍隊現代化，也持續挑戰英國依《甘達馬克條約》取得的對外權力。英方的政治與戰略中樞在英屬印度政府，俾路支及奎達方向由雷金納德·戴爾中將統籌；威廉·斯萊姆則指揮第三拉合爾步兵旅，該旅包括第十五盧迪亞納錫克步兵第一營、第四十七錫克步兵第一營、第四廓爾喀步槍第二營及第六十九旁遮普步兵營。斯萊姆所部特別適應崎嶇道路、接連攻佔山口和迅速鞏固新據點的工作。亨利·麥克馬洪爵士代表英印方面主持政治談判。7月19日哈比布拉汗遇刺身亡，穆罕默德·納迪爾沙隨後接任埃米爾，並在既有軍敗局勢下接受英方的外交條件。
peopleEn: The Afghan commander-in-chief was Emir Habibullah Khan. Ruling since 1901, he sought to modernize the national army while continuing to challenge the power that Britain retained over Afghan foreign relations under the Treaty of Gandamak. The British political and strategic center lay with the Government of India; Reginald Dyer coordinated the Baluchistan and Quetta approaches, while William Slim commanded the 3rd (Lahore) Infantry Brigade. The brigade included the 1st Battalion, 15th Ludhiana Sikhs; the 1st Battalion, 47th Sikhs; the 2nd Battalion, 4th Gurkha Rifles; and the 69th Punjabis. Slim’s formation was particularly suited to movement along difficult tracks, the seizure of successive passes, and the rapid consolidation of newly taken positions. Sir Henry McMahon represented the Indian government in the political negotiations. Habibullah was assassinated on 19 July, after which Muhammad Nadir Shah succeeded him and accepted British diplomatic terms in the context of the military defeat.
kits: 英軍與印軍的主要步槍是.303英制口徑長槍李-恩菲爾德第三型及短槍李-恩菲爾德第一型，兩者均使用十發可拆卸彈匣；英軍還配備維克斯一型重機槍，以連續彈鏈供應，Lewis .303輕機槍則適合近距離快速射擊。印度炮兵使用十三磅與十八磅野戰砲，步兵連亦配三英吋迫擊砲，十八磅砲可發射榴彈及霰彈，手榴彈則有1915年列裝的米爾斯第五型。皇家航空隊出動已列裝的de Havilland DH.9巡邏機及Handley Page O/400轟炸機。阿軍前線可見.577/.450 Martini-Henry舊式步槍及部分英制.303 Lee-Enfield步槍，兩種口徑的彈藥不能通用，這直接增加其後勤與戰術限制。英軍補給由鐵路終點接上汽車隊，再以騾隊沿狹窄山徑分載砲件、彈藥、機槍附件和飲水；前線指揮所則以野戰電話、無線電及飛機觀察砲兵射界。
kitsEn: The principal infantry weapons of the British and Indian troops were the .303-inch Long Lee-Enfield Mk III and Short Lee-Enfield Mk I, both using ten-round detachable box magazines. British units also had the water-cooled Vickers Mk I machine gun supplied by continuous ammunition belts, while the .303-inch Lewis gun provided rapid close-range fire. Indian artillery included the 13-pounder and 18-pounder field guns, with a 3-inch mortar available to infantry; the 18-pounder fired high-explosive and shrapnel shells, and the Mills Bomb No. 5, introduced in 1915, was the standard British fragmentation grenade. The Royal Air Force employed the already-service de Havilland DH.9 reconnaissance aircraft and Handley Page O/400 bombers. Afghan troops in the line were seen with older .577/.450 Martini-Henry rifles as well as some British .303-inch Lee-Enfield rifles, and the incompatible ammunition imposed real logistical and tactical limitations. British supply moved from railway termini by motor lorries and was then divided among mule teams along narrow mountain tracks to carry gun components, ammunition, machine-gun equipment, and water. Brigade headquarters connected field telephones, wireless, and artillery observation with the aircraft.
tactics: 開戰之初，阿軍以步兵沿山徑攻擊巴米揚及外圍英軍據點，並威脅霍斯特、塔普坎方向；英軍先放棄過度突出的陣位，把兵力集中到庫拉姆、皮欣與奎達的可補給地區。五月二十二日，庫拉姆縱隊在炮火與飛機觀察支援下越過低庫拉姆，奪取塔普坎；同時，皮欣方向部隊由查曼經皮欣及阿爾甘達布河谷向哈里河推進，在古利斯坦一帶與阿軍接觸。英軍沒有沿單一大路直推，而是以步兵控制山脊和河口，砲兵觀察後集中火力，機槍組封鎖道路與退路，騎兵僅在可通行谷地追擊，再由騾隊維持每日糧彈。英軍雖在可調集兵力與重炮上占優，仍採取逐步推進、鞏固據點、再向前探察的節奏；飛機則協助發現阿軍縱隊、標定砲火及轟擊陣地。阿軍曾利用山嶺、壕溝、岩石胸牆與夜襲反擊，使英軍不能僅靠一次正面衝鋒取得道路。英軍在古利斯坦及霍斯特方向切斷阿軍各部聯繫，五月底占領霍斯特；六月七日努魯茲一役中，阿軍反攻未能扭轉局勢，陣地與裝備隨後被英軍控制。此後英軍有能力向喀布爾方向推進，卻選擇鞏固前線並等待外交決定。
tacticsEn: At the opening of the campaign, Afghan infantry moved along mountain tracks to attack Bamiyan and the British outposts, while threatening the Khost and Tapkan approaches. The British first withdrew from overextended positions and concentrated their troops at Kurram, Pishin, and Quetta, where supplies could be maintained. On 22 May, the Kurram column crossed Low Kurram under artillery fire and aerial observation and seized Tapkan. At the same time, troops moving from Pishin advanced through Chaman, Pishin, and the Arghandab valley toward the Hari River and engaged Afghan forces around Gulistan. The British did not simply drive along one road. Infantry held ridges and river crossings, artillery registered targets before concentrating fire, machine-gun teams covered roads and withdrawals, cavalry pursued only where the ground permitted, and mule trains carried the daily ration and ammunition. Although the British could bring more troops and heavy guns into action, they advanced by bounds, consolidated each position, and then reconnoitred farther. Aircraft helped locate Afghan columns, correct artillery fire, and strike troop positions. The Afghans used ridges, trenches, rock-cut breastworks, and night attacks to prevent the British from taking a road in a single frontal assault. British operations around Gulistan and Khost disrupted Afghan contact, and the British occupied Khost late in May. At Nowruz on 7 June, an Afghan counterattack failed to reverse the situation, and the position and its equipment subsequently fell to British control. The British then had the capacity to advance toward Kabul, but chose to consolidate the forward line and await a diplomatic settlement.
data: 作戰時間線可核對的節點如下：5月6日，阿軍在巴米揚及其他前線據點發動攻擊，英軍遂逐步收縮外圍陣地；五月初英印當局向喀布爾提出限期要求，未獲接受後，正式軍事進攻獲准展開。5月22日，庫拉姆方向發生塔普坎戰鬥，英軍奪取陣地；其後數日，皮欣縱隊在古利斯坦及哈里河一線推進。五月二十日至三十一日，霍斯特與周邊高地先後易手，英軍控制東南進入阿軍側翼的道路。6月7日，努魯茲爆發此次戰爭最後一場大規模地面交戰，英軍獲勝，阿軍主力退離前線。6月起，喀布爾提出停火與談判，軍事行動則縮減為鞏固既有據點。7月19日，哈比布拉汗遇刺身亡；納迪爾沙接任後批准談判。8月8日，條約在拉瓦爾品第簽訂，通常即以該日作為戰爭終點。各方傷亡數字因是否計入作戰、疾病、事故及不同統計口徑而差異甚大，因此不宜引用一個看似精確的總數。
dataEn: The verifiable chronology runs as follows. On 6 May, Afghan forces attacked Bamiyan and other forward positions, prompting the British to contract their outposts. After the British-Indian authorities issued an ultimatum to Kabul in early May and did not receive an acceptable answer, the full military offensive was authorized. On 22 May, the Battle of Tapkan was fought in the Kurram sector, and the British took the position. During the following days, the Pishin column advanced through the Gulistan and Hari River area. Between 20 and 31 May, Khost and the surrounding heights changed hands, giving the British control of the roads by which Afghan formations could be turned. On 7 June, the last major land engagement of the war was fought at Nowruz. The British won, and the main Afghan force withdrew from the forward area. From June, Kabul sought a ceasefire and negotiations while military activity narrowed to the consolidation of existing positions. Habibullah was assassinated on 19 July, and Nadir Shah approved the negotiations after taking the throne. The treaty was signed at Rawalpindi on 8 August, conventionally taken as the end of the war. Published casualty totals vary according to whether they include combat losses, disease, accidents, and different reporting definitions, so no single apparently exact total can be used with confidence.
cause: 第三次英阿戰爭不是單純的邊界衝突，而是國家主權、邊境安全與帝國政策交疊造成的戰爭。1879年《甘達馬克條約》使阿富汗在內政仍由喀布爾自治的情況下，把外交權及其與印度的關係置於英國控制之下；此後歷代埃米爾與英國之間始終存在權限爭議。哈比布拉汗一面擴充軍隊，一面希望收回更多外交自主。第一次世界大戰期間，英方尤其擔心阿富汗利用英屬印度的反英政治運動削弱英國在西北邊疆的統治，並認為德國方面的情報活動可能與喀布爾建立聯繫。五月初，阿軍在巴米揚及邊境據點的攻擊使原本可由外交處理的爭端迅速軍事化；英印當局隨後要求停止對英屬印度事務的干預，並要求喀布爾接受英方對外政策與安全保證。阿方未接受全部要求，英軍遂以三個方向進攻，目標既是奪取邊境陣地，也是迫使哈比布拉汗在外交上讓步。
causeEn: The Third Anglo-Afghan War was not merely a frontier clash. It arose from the collision of state sovereignty, frontier security, and imperial policy. The Treaty of Gandamak of 1879 had left Afghanistan internally administered from Kabul but placed its foreign relations and relations with India under British control, and successive Afghan rulers continued to dispute the limits of that arrangement. Habibullah expanded the army while seeking a greater measure of diplomatic independence. During the First World War, the British were particularly concerned that Afghanistan might exploit anti-British political activity in British India to weaken British authority on the North-West Frontier, and they believed German intelligence activity might establish contacts with Kabul. In early May, Afghan attacks on Bamiyan and the frontier outposts transformed a dispute that might have been handled diplomatically into an immediate military emergency. The British-Indian authorities then demanded an end to interference in Indian affairs and acceptance of British requirements concerning foreign policy and security. Kabul did not accept all the terms, so the British attack from three directions was designed both to capture frontier positions and to force Habibullah into diplomatic concessions.
impact: 拉瓦爾品第條約把軍事失敗轉化為長期制度約束：阿富汗不再能自行決定對英屬印度的政策，英國取得在認為必要時派兵介入阿富汗的權利，並可在 Afghan territory調動軍隊與戰略物資。這使阿富汗的內政仍由喀布爾處理，卻大幅削弱其對外自主與戰時籌碼，也使英國在西北邊疆取得比單純據點更有利的戰略保證。條約沒有正式宣布吞併阿富汗，英軍亦未占領喀布爾，因此這不是殖民政權的建立；但外交權受制已是制度性變化。哈比布拉汗的軍政威望因戰敗而崩解，其後繼者納迪爾沙轉向依靠英國重建軍隊，英國武器、訓練與貸款於是成為阿富汗軍現代化的重要來源。空軍對喀布爾軍事設施的襲擊也顯示首都已可受到英方空中壓力。對英屬印度而言，西北邊疆的直接軍事壓力暫時下降，但英國仍須承擔邊防、軍援及監察阿富汗的成本。
impactEn: The Treaty of Rawalpindi converted a military defeat into a lasting institutional constraint. Afghanistan could no longer determine its policy toward British India independently; Britain acquired the right to intervene militarily whenever it considered necessary and to move troops and strategic material through Afghan territory. Afghanistan retained domestic administration in Kabul, but its diplomatic autonomy and bargaining power were sharply reduced, giving Britain strategic guarantees more valuable than the occupation of a few forward positions. The treaty did not formally annex Afghanistan, and British troops did not occupy Kabul, so this was not the creation of a colonial government. Nevertheless, the restriction of foreign relations represented a structural change. Habibullah’s military and political prestige collapsed after the defeat, and his successor Nadir Shah turned toward Britain to rebuild the Afghan army, making British weapons, training, and loans important to Afghan military modernization. Air attacks on Afghan military facilities in Kabul also demonstrated that the capital itself could be subjected to British air pressure. The immediate military pressure on India’s North-West Frontier declined, although Britain still carried the costs of frontier defense, military assistance, and supervision of Afghanistan.
result: 努魯茲戰鬥後，阿軍放棄東南主要前線，英軍控制霍斯特及通往喀布爾的接近道路，但沒有向首都展開占領式進攻。經過六月至七月的談判，哈比布拉汗遇刺身亡及納迪爾沙即位改變了阿方代表，卻沒有改變核心條件。8月8日簽訂的《拉瓦爾品第條約》規定：阿富汗停止干涉英屬印度事務；英國在認為必要時保留軍事介入阿富汗的權利；阿方須維持對英友好並為英國政治及商務代表提供便利；英國軍隊與戰略物資可經阿富汗通行；阿方須為英印當局採購糧食、徵用運輸及其他補給提供便利；英國則承諾不干涉阿富汗內政。結果是英國取得明確的軍事與外交勝利，但勝利表現在迫使喀布爾接受條約、限制其行動自由，而非征服首都或兼併國土。因史料統計範圍不一，這場戰爭不宜列出一組未經核實的精確傷亡數字。
resultEn: After the fighting at Nowruz, the Afghan army abandoned its principal southeastern front, and the British controlled Khost and the approaches toward Kabul without beginning an occupation of the capital. Negotiations continued through June and July. The assassination of Habibullah and the accession of Nadir Shah changed the Afghan signatories but not the essential terms. The Treaty of Rawalpindi, signed on 8 August, required Afghanistan to cease interference in the affairs of British India; reserved to Britain the right to intervene militarily whenever it considered necessary; obliged the Afghan government to maintain friendly relations and provide facilities for British political and commercial agents; allowed British troops and strategic material to pass through Afghan territory; required full Afghan assistance for the purchase of provisions, transport, and other supplies for the British and Indian governments; and pledged Britain not to interfere in Afghan internal affairs. The result was a clear British military and diplomatic victory, expressed through Kabul’s acceptance of the treaty and the restriction of its freedom of action rather than through the conquest of the capital or the annexation of Afghan territory. Because surviving statistics use different scopes, no single unverified set of precise casualty figures should be presented for the war.
